purpose: Manufacturer-verified records for Lantronix Open-M 720G and Open-M 520G production-ready system-on-modules based on MediaTek Genio 720/520, with emphasis on low-power edge GenAI and local inference constraints.
notes: Lantronix markets both modules for edge AI/GenAI and states module-class power below 4 W; this is not a complete carrier-board or end-system wall-power measurement.
MediaTek documents TFLite Generative AI acceleration on the NPU for Genio 520/720 under Android and Yocto. ONNX Runtime is currently documented for analytical AI, not as a general ORT-GenAI path.

The full NeuroPilot 8 SDK bundle is access-controlled. Public developers can use supported LiteRT/TFLite delegate paths, but arbitrary GGUF/llama.cpp compatibility must not be inferred from the 10-TOPS headline.
No public per-unit Lantronix pricing was found; current purchasing is contact-sales/quote based.

hardware.cpu: 2x Arm Cortex-A78 up to 2.6 GHz + 6x Arm Cortex-A55 up to 2.0 GHz
hardware.gpu: Arm Mali-G57 MC2 up to 1.1 GHz
hardware.ai_compute_metric_note: Lantronix and MediaTek describe up to 10 TOPS of system AI acceleration. TOPS is not treated as an LLM token-generation benchmark.

power.notes: Lantronix advertises efficient power below 4 W for the SOM family. Carrier-board, peripherals, radios and workload-dependent system power are additional.

hardware.genai_runtime_support: MediaTek IoT AI Hub currently documents TFLite Generative AI execution on the NPU for Genio 520/720 under Android and Yocto. General ONNX Runtime GenAI is not documented as the supported GAI path; MediaTek directs GAI workloads to the NeuroPilot GAI Toolkit/TFLite stack.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: Runtime-specific. Do not infer arbitrary GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ or INT4 support from the 10-TOPS figure. Supported model conversion, precision and operator coverage should be verified against the current NeuroPilot 8 GAI toolchain for the exact model.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 8 GB of shared system memory makes this primarily a compact edge-GenAI platform. Small 1B-3B-class models are the safest capacity target; selected 7B-class models may fit only with aggressive low-bit quantization and constrained context/runtime overhead. Fit does not imply useful NPU acceleration unless the model is supported by MediaTek's GAI toolchain.
hardware.performance_per_watt: promising_for_supported_edge_models_due_to_sub_4w_module_class_power, but no normalized public LLM tokens-per-watt benchmark was found
hardware.off_grid_suitability: very_high_potential; sub-4 W module-class power and 3.7 V nominal input are attractive for battery/solar designs, but carrier-board and peripheral consumption must be added

pricing.note: Lantronix lists the production-ready SOM and part number but does not publish a stable unit price.

hardware.cpu: 2x Arm Cortex-A78 up to 2.2 GHz + 6x Arm Cortex-A55 up to 2.0 GHz
hardware.gpu: Arm Mali-G57 MC2 up to 880 MHz
hardware.ai_compute_metric_note: Lantronix and MediaTek describe up to 10 TOPS of system AI acceleration. TOPS is not treated as an LLM token-generation benchmark.

hardware.genai_runtime_support: MediaTek IoT AI Hub documents TFLite Generative AI execution on the NPU for Genio 520/720 under Android and Yocto. The specialized GAI toolchain is distinct from unrestricted desktop GGUF runtimes.

hardware.model_size_practicality: 4 GB shared memory sharply limits language-model capacity. Best suited to sub-3B compact models, speech/vision pipelines, embeddings and task-specific GenAI models supported by MediaTek's deployment toolchain. Larger models generally require more memory or host-assisted execution.
